claims.head: Iron sharpens iron
claims.body: The Red Wings are one of the league’s best for the power play, but the Panthers are one of the best at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Red Wings’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots. The Panthers take a lot of penalties and the Red Wings draw plenty of them, so their power play should get its chances.

FLA.head: The Panthers have a slight edge
FLA.body: The two have been about even at out-chancing opponents lately. Florida has home-ice advantage, but they will be without Barkov. Still, it’s close: the Red Wings can make it interesting if they keep dangerous shots away.

DET.head: A slightly uphill night for the Red Wings
DET.body: The two have been about even at out-chancing opponents lately. Florida has home-ice advantage, but they will be without Barkov. The Red Wings’ best way to tip it is keeping dangerous shots away.

story.head: DeBrincat’s favorite opponent
paras: The Panthers have won three straight, and the Red Wings have won two in a row. This is an Atlantic Division matchup, with the Red Wings last (tied for 16th in the NHL) and the Panthers third (tied for sixth). The Atlantic has been the strongest of the four divisions so far.

The Red Wings have played better than their record (.577) says: their chances are worth about .634, and their finishing has held them back. The Panthers’ record (.643) is about what their chances are worth.

The Red Wings block more shots than almost anyone (2nd) and draw more penalties than they take (2nd). They also have one of the league’s most dangerous power plays (3rd), and their power play against the Panthers’ penalty killers is strength against strength. On the other side, the Cats forecheck harder than anyone (1st), rarely ice the puck (1st) and hit a lot (1st). Both teams play slow, low-event hockey, so expect a tight one.

Alex DeBrincat (6 G / 9 A / 15 P in 13 GP) leads the Red Wings in scoring, with a point in seven straight games against Florida. Viktor Arvidsson (8 G / 6 A / 14 P in 13 GP) has a team-high eight goals, with nine points in his last five games. Matthew Tkachuk (4 G / 16 A / 20 P in 14 GP) leads the Panthers in scoring and is tied for seventh in the NHL, and Brady Tkachuk (8 G / 7 A / 15 P in 14 GP) has a team-high eight goals.
John Gibson (4-4-1 / .874 SV% in 9 GS) will likely start for Detroit, and Akira Schmid (5-2-1 / .888 SV% in 7 GS) for Florida.

items.text: The Panthers have been without Jacob Markström, Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand for several games. Akira Schmid is expected to start.
The Red Wings are newly without Dylan Larkin, have been without Marco Kasper and Mason Appleton for several games, and have had to make do without Jacob Bernard-Docker all season.
With Dylan Larkin out, Emmitt Finnie took 14 faceoffs in the Red Wings’ last game. He had been taking about three a game.
Carter Verhaeghe has eight goals on chances worth about 4.5 goals, well above what his finishing usually turns chances into. Runs like that tend to cool off.
